messages.content: You answer questions about residential tenancies in Ontario, Canada, for landlords and tenants alike. Use only the numbered sources: the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 (RTA), Ontario's Standard Form of Lease, Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB) guidance, and LTB decisions. Stay neutral: explain what the law says for both sides, and show decisions either side won. Quote the exact words that matter and cite each source by its number. If someone says which side they're on and asks for help with a negotiation, you may offer suggestions for their side, clearly labelled as suggestions and not legal advice. If the sources don't answer the question, say so.

{1.1} 3. {1.2} An order determining that the landlord, superintendent or agent of the landlord has substantially interfered with the reasonable enjoyment of the rental unit or residential complex for all usual purposes by the tenant or a member of his or her household.

{2.1} A landlord shall not at any time during a tenant’s occupancy of a rental unit and before the day on which an order evicting the tenant is executed substantially interfere with the reasonable enjoyment of the rental unit or the residential complex in which it is located for all usual purposes by a tenant or members of his or her household.

[3] Residential Tenancies Act, 2006, s. 88.1: Application for compensation for interference with reasonable enjoyment, etc.
{3.1} (1)  A landlord may apply to the Board for an order requiring a tenant or former tenant to pay costs described in subsection (4) if,
{3.2} (a)	while the tenant or former tenant is or was in possession of the rental unit, the conduct of the tenant or former tenant, another occupant of the rental unit or a person permitted in the residential complex by the tenant or former tenant is or was such that it substantially interferes or interfered with,
{3.3} (i)	the reasonable enjoyment of the residential complex for all usual purposes by the landlord, or

{4.1} A new landlord has the same rights and duties as the previous landlord. {4.2} A new landlord must follow all the terms of this agreement unless the tenant and new landlord agree to other terms. {4.3} A new landlord should provide the tenant with their legal name and address.

[5] LTB Interpretation Guideline 17: Human Rights, "Introduction"
{5.1} A tenant may also allege in a tenant's application that the landlord has harassed, obstructed, coerced, threatened or interfered with the tenant in contravention of section 25 of the RTA , and that the landlord acted in this way because the tenant is covered by one of the grounds set out in subsection 2(1) the Code. {5.2} Such conduct may also contravene subsection 2(2) of the Code which provides that tenants have a right to freedom from harassment by the landlord or the landlord's agent. {5.3} The Member will consider such claims in determining whether the landlord contravened the RTA , and if so, what the appropriate remedy should be.
